entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 5 Jr 5:1-31 . The Cause of the Judgments to Be Inflicted Is the Universal Corruption of the People. 1. a man-- As the pious Josiah, Baruch, and Zephaniah lived in Jerusalem at that time, Jeremiah must here mean the mass of the people, the king, his counsellors, the false prophets, and the priests, as distinguished from the faithful few, whom God had openly separated from the reprobate people; among the latter not even one just person was to be found ( Is 9:16 ) [Calvin]; the godly, moreover, were forbidden to intercede for them ( Jr 7:16 ; compare Ge 18:23 , &c.; Psa 12:1 ; Eze 22:30 ). see ... know-- look ... ascertain. judgment-- justice, righteousness. pardon it-- rather, her.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9689"/><div sID="gen17102" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9689"/><hi type="bold">8. in the morning--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.5.11">Is 5:11</reference>). "Rising early in the morning" is a phrase for unceasing eagerness in any pursuit; such was the Jews' avidity after idol-worship. Maurer translates from a different Hebrew root, "continually wander to and fro," inflamed with lust (<reference osisRef="Jer.2.23">Jr 2:23</reference>). But English Version is simpler (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.13.27">Jr 13:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.22.11">Eze 22:11</reference>). <div eID="gen17102" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9700"/><div sID="gen17124" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9700"/>19. Retribution in kind. As ye have forsaken Me (<reference osisRef="Jer.2.13">Jr 2:13</reference>), so shall ye be forsaken by Me. As ye have served strange (foreign) gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers (foreigners) in a land not yours. Compare the similar retribution in <reference osisRef="Deut.28.47">De 28:47</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.28.48">48</reference>. <div eID="gen17124" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9703"/><div sID="gen17127" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9703"/>23. (<reference osisRef="Jer.6.28">Jr 6:28</reference>). <div eID="gen17127" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9704"/><div sID="gen17128" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9704"/><hi type="bold">24. rain ... former ... latter--</hi>The "former" falls from the middle of October to the beginning of December. The "latter," or spring rain in Palestine, falls before harvest in March and April, and is essential for ripening the crops (<reference osisRef="Deut.11.14">De 11:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.2.23">Joe 2:23</reference>).<div eID="gen17128" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17129" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">weeks of ... harvest--</hi>the seven weeks between passover and pentecost, beginning on the sixteenth of Nisan (<reference osisRef="Deut.16.9">De 16:9</reference>). By God's special providence no rain fell in Palestine during the harvest weeks, so that harvest work went on without interruption (see <reference osisRef="Gen.8.22">Ge 8:22</reference>). <div eID="gen17129" type="x-p"/>
